detected_by: wc -l on the batch log stayed at 0 far longer than the measured per-unit cost implied, then ps aux showed java invocations still pointing at the prior batch's settings dir after the fixtures had been overwritten
impact: regenerated .pcg fixtures in place (same filenames) while a prior background xargs batch against those same files was still mid-flight, then launched a second parallel batch on top without stopping the first; two overlapping PCGen batches (12+8 concurrent JVMs) briefly ran against a shared box already under sibling-lane load, and one batch's log showed a completed slug that a later grep also found still running under the OLD settings dir
resolution: TaskStop on both background bash tasks, pkill -9 on every java process under this agent's own scratch PCGen build path (confirmed no sibling processes matched), wiped the oracle-txt output dir, and reran once cleanly at lower parallelism
